1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D pixel MotoGP manager game for phone/tablet, featuring the full MotoGP rider grid and motorcycles.

## Requirements
- User: “2D Pixel MotoGP manager full rider MotoGP and motorcycle motogp (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)”
- Build the full playable game immediately; do not ask clarifying questions; briefly note assumptions at the end.
- Use responsive touch layouts for Android/iOS phones and tablets.
- Save verification screenshots as small JPEGs with viewport width ≤1280px; read only the latest image; use full-size PNG only for fine detail.

## Decisions
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS plus Canvas, no build step or external runtime dependencies.
- Uses the 2025 22-rider/11-team grid, 14-round fan season, real circuit names, 10-lap compressed races.
- Includes rider/team selection, tyres, setups, 3-tap qualifying mini-game, starting grid, live race strategy, pit stop, points, championship standings, bike upgrades, multi-season career, localStorage save.
- Self-hosted “Press Start 2P” font; fan-made/non-commercial disclaimer added.
- Assumptions: “full grid” means 2025 entrants; race handling is management-based with automated riding and player pace/tyre/pit calls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full game shell and screens: title, team/rider selection, paddock hub, briefing, qualifying, grid, race, results, standings, garage, season end.
- 22 riders, 11 teams, 14 circuits with SVG path maps, pixel bikes/helmets, live top-down Canvas race.
- Race simulation: countdown lights, AI field, pace modes, tyre wear, fuel, pit stop, DNF-free finish, results, points/prizes.
- Career systems: transfers not included, but upgrades, credits, standings, seasons, career stats, reset/save.
- Fixed boot-order error (`stopQualiLoop is not defined`).
- Fixed modal clicks being blocked by inline `stopPropagation`.
- Fixed `P1ST` display bug; ordinal now returns `P1`.
- Fixed huge garage stat bars caused by inline `.meter`; added `display:block`.
- Limited desktop bottom nav width to 760px.
- Added fallback bright map color for dark-team liveries.
- Widened race track curbs; sponsor boards added.
- Verified on mobile and desktop: new career, sign rider, hub, briefing, qualifying, grid, race, pit, results, standings, garage.
- All files syntax-checked with `node --check`.

### Active
- Improving race-track visuals: red/white kerbs still appear mostly white in screenshots; sampled Canvas reported `red: 817`, `white: 279692`, indicating red curb segments are effectively not visible.
- Current browser is on the race screen at 1280×900 with the race paused and `raceRAF` canceled for screenshot capture.
- Gameplay balance still needs a full end-to-end race and season test.

### Blocked
- None technically; remaining work is verification and visual polish.

## Next Move
1. Fix track kerbs visibly: draw explicit alternating red/white edge segments or otherwise guarantee red curb pixels; re-capture race at desktop and phone sizes.
2. Resume/finish a complete race normally and verify results → paddock → standings → garage upgrade → next race.
3. Test season end by advancing/setting `state.round` near `TOTAL_ROUNDS`, verify champion/title/new-season flow.
4. Test team standings tab, upgrade purchase, reset-career flow, and reload persistence.
5. Check 390×844, 430×932, 768×1024, and 1280×900 layouts; verify no clipping/overflow.
6. Optionally inspect title/select/briefing/qualifying visually after latest CSS changes.
7. Commit changes when satisfied; currently all changes are uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: page shell and script load order (`data.js`, `core.js`, `screens.js`, `quali.js`, `race.js`).
- `styles.css`: entire responsive pixel UI; recent fixes for nav, meters, race layout.
- `js/data.js`: teams, 22 riders, circuits, tyres, setups, pace modes, points.
- `js/core.js`: storage, derived ratings, SVG helpers, chrome, title, routing, modal/toast.
- `js/screens.js`: team select, hub, briefing, standings, garage, results, season end.
- `js/quali.js`: 3-tap qualifying and grid.
- `js/race.js`: race engine, HUD, track canvas, final classification; boot call at end.
- `assets/fonts/PressStart2P.ttf` and `assets/fonts/OFL.txt`: self-hosted pixel font/license.
- `screenshots/race-desktop.jpg`: latest race visual issue reference.
- `screenshots/garage-desktop2.jpg`: latest garage layout.
- `screenshots/hub-desktop.jpg`: desktop hub reference.
- `screenshots/results-mobile2.jpg`: latest results reference.
- `screenshots/grid-mobile2.jpg`: latest grid reference.

## Important Context
- Server running in tmux session `motogp` at `http://127.0.0.1:3002`.
- Use cache-busted URLs such as `?v=9` after JS/CSS changes because the static server caches scripts.
- Race screenshots timeout unless the render loop is stopped first: `playwright-cli eval "() => { if(raceRAF) cancelAnimationFrame(raceRAF); raceRAF=null; }"`.
- Playwright browser is open at 1280×900 in the race view; reload to resume from saved career.
- Save key: `motogp-pixel-manager-v1`; current saved career is Jorge Martin / Aprilia, round 0.
- Race/session state is intentionally not persisted; reload returns to title with the saved career.
- Canvas race sampling used `ctx.getImageData()` and showed red curbs absent despite source order `red stroke → white dashed stroke → asphalt`.
- Known minor polish item: pit stop is severe because freezing 3.2s in a 10-lap compressed race can drop many positions; consider reducing pit duration if testing reveals frustration.
